findings.title: No authorization check for team/org delegated credentials
findings.body: The deleteCache handler only checks `credential.userId === user.id`, but credentials can be delegated or team-owned (as seen elsewhere with delegationCredentialId handling). This check doesn't account for delegated credentials or admin-managed credentials, potentially blocking legitimate admin deletions or allowing inconsistent authorization behavior compared to other credential-related handlers (e.g. disconnect) that may use a shared permission check.

findings.title: Generic Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: Throwing a plain `Error` instead of `TRPCError` with a proper code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND` or `UNAUTHORIZED`) means the client will receive a generic 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a meaningful error code, making it harder for clients to distinguish between 'not found' and other failures, and this is inconsistent with other handlers in the codebase using TRPCError.

findings.title: updatedAt default violates @updatedAt semantics / inconsistent with schema default
findings.body: The migration sets `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` but the Prisma schema marks the field `@default(now()) @updatedAt`. Prisma's @updatedAt expects the column to auto-update on every write via Prisma Client, but any direct SQL writes/upserts bypassing Prisma (e.g. raw queries) will not update this field automatically, and existing rows retroactively get 'NOW()' as updatedAt at migration time which is misleading since it doesn't reflect actual last-cache-update time, undermining the newly added cache-status UI feature.

findings.title: cacheUpdatedAt may already be a Date, double wrapping with new Date()
findings.body: `cacheUpdatedAt` is typed `Date | null` but comes over tRPC (serialized via superjson, so likely fine) — however calling `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` when cacheUpdatedAt is already a Date object is redundant but not harmful. More importantly, `hasCache` check `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` doesn't account for `cacheUpdatedAt` being `undefined` vs `null`, and the dropdown won't render if cache does not yet exist even though 'isGoogleCalendar' is true, which may be the intended early return but should be verified against the full feature matrix (e.g. integrations other than Google Calendar relying on cache).

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds called on every connectedCalendars query without caching
findings.body: `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` on every request to `connectedCalendars`, adding an additional groupBy query per request. For users/orgs with many credentials this could add noticeable DB load; there's no memoization or batching optimization, and this new query runs regardless of whether the UI actually needs cache status (e.g., non-Google calendar integrations).

findings.title: cacheUpdatedAt uses || null, converting falsy-but-valid timestamps incorrectly
findings.body: `cacheStatusMap.get(calendar.credentialId) || null` will treat a valid Date object as falsy only if it's literally falsy, which Date objects never are, so this isn't actually buggy for Date values — but it silently swallows the distinction between 'no cache status found' and 'found but value is null', which could mask bugs if getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ever returns `{credentialId, updatedAt: undefined}`. Low risk but worth tightening to explicit undefined check for clarity and correctness guarantees.
